options: Confirming that output meets customer satisfaction standards
Discovering problems or bugs in processes or code, during or after implementation
Training end-users on a new system
questions.explanation: Testing is about discovering problems or bugs in processes or code, either during or after implementation.

options: Finding bugs in individual code units
Making sure the standards and output of processes or solutions meet customer satisfaction
Checking the speed of database queries
questions.explanation: QA is about making sure that the standards and output of processes or solutions meet customer satisfaction and expected quality.

questions.stem: Which stage of testing checks individual parts?
questions.explanation: Unit Testing checks individual parts; System Integration Testing verifies components work together; User Acceptance Testing ensures the solution meets user requirements.

questions.stem: Which stage of testing ensures the solution meets user requirements?
questions.explanation: User Acceptance Testing ensures the solution meets user requirements.

questions.stem: In the example of a table with a million rows of country names, what would QA catch that testing might not?
options: Inconsistent spellings of country names or non-uniform data formats
That the table has the wrong number of columns
That the query runs too slowly
That the server ran out of disk space
questions.explanation: Testing might confirm all million rows are present, but QA would catch inconsistent spellings or non-uniform data formats.

questions.stem: According to the comparison of testing and QA, what do many project failures result from?
options: Poor QA processes rather than bad testing
questions.explanation: Many project failures result from poor QA processes rather than bad testing.

questions.stem: Why does data quality become especially crucial in the era of unstructured data?
options: Because unstructured data is always smaller in volume
Because unstructured data never contains errors
Because numerous checks and fixes are needed, and if end-users cannot trust the data, having it becomes pointless
Because unstructured data does not need testing
questions.explanation: Unstructured data requires numerous checks and fixes to maintain quality; if end-users cannot trust the quality, having the data is pointless.

questions.stem: What is described as the ultimate factor for a successful implementation?
options: The size of the testing team
questions.explanation: Business satisfaction is the ultimate factor for a successful implementation.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the relationship between testing and QA?
options: QA replaces testing once a project goes live
Testing is more important than QA for any system
QA is only needed for unstructured data
Testing and QA are the same activity under different names
Testing finds bugs, while QA ensures the solution meets the standards and quality expected by users
questions.explanation: Testing finds bugs; QA ensures the solution not only functions correctly but also meets the desired standards and quality expected by users.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a stage of testing during an IT project?
options: Checking individual parts of the code
questions.explanation: The stages listed are Unit Testing, System Integration Testing and User Acceptance Testing; customer satisfaction is the concern of QA, not a named testing stage.
